# adsb.aero

Historical ADS-B flight trajectory search. Every flight is a full 4D trajectory
(position + altitude + time, plus track, ground speed, vertical rate, IAS and
squawk as time series), ingested from the adsb.lol global archive.

This file is the complete guide to the HTTP API. If you read only this, you can
write correct queries. Machine-readable schema: <https://adsb.aero/api/openapi.json>
(56 KB — you probably don't need it). Human docs: <https://adsb.aero/api/docs>.

- **Base URL**: `https://adsb.aero/api/v1`
- **Auth**: none. Public read-only data.
- **Content type**: `application/json`. CORS is open to all origins.
- **Be polite**: this runs on one box. Prefer one broad query over many narrow
  ones, keep `limit` modest, and don't poll in a loop.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/query` | Search flights. The main endpoint. |
| GET | `/airports/{code}` | **Resolve an ICAO/IATA code to a position _and_ its aerodrome airspace polygons.** |
| GET | `/waypoints/search?q=` | Typeahead over airports, navaids, VFR reporting points, airspaces. |
| GET | `/waypoints/{id}` | One waypoint by OpenAIP ID. |
| GET | `/airspaces?pos=lat,lng&dist=` | Airspaces near a point (`dist` in km, max 100). |
| GET | `/flights/{flight_id}` | Full trajectory for one flight. |
| GET | `/data-range` | `first_date` / `last_date` actually held. Check this before assuming coverage. |
| GET | `/icao-types?start=&end=` | Aircraft types seen in a date range, with counts. |
| GET | `/health` | Liveness. |

## Start here: departures and arrivals

This is the most common question ("who flew into X?", "where do people arriving
at X come from?"), and the way to get it right is not obvious.

There is **no `departs_from`/`arrives_at` predicate and no airport-code filter.**
Endpoints are expressed geometrically: a flight arrived at X if its last position
falls inside a geometry around X.

**Use the aerodrome's published airspace, not a radius.** `GET /airports/{code}`
returns the ATZ / MATZ / CTR polygons whose boundary contains the field. That
boundary is the real, correctly-sized, correctly-shaped extent of the aerodrome —
a guessed radius is too big for a grass strip and too small for a major hub, and
it is circular when real airspace usually isn't.

Step 1 — resolve the code:

```bash
curl https://adsb.aero/api/v1/airports/EGHP
```

```jsonc
{
  "ident": "EGHP", "name": "POPHAM", "lon": -1.2347, "lat": 51.1936,
  "elevation_ft": 550,
  "airspaces": [                      // most specific (smallest) first
    {
      "name": "POPHAM ATZ", "type_name": "ATZ", "area_km2": 7.1,
      "lower_limit": {"value": 0,    "unit": "ft", "ref": "gnd"},
      "upper_limit": {"value": 2550, "unit": "ft", "ref": "msl"},
      "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[...]]]}
    }
  ]
}
```

Step 2 — paste `airspaces[0].geometry` straight into the query:

```bash
curl -X POST https://adsb.aero/api/v1/query \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "match": {
      "endpoint_within": {
        "mode": "end",
        "geometry": { "type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[...]]] }
      }
    },
    "end_date": "2026-09-12T00:00:00Z",
    "window_days": 7,
    "limit": 100,
    "include_path": false
  }'
```

Use `"mode": "start"` for departures, `"end"` for arrivals, `"both"` for
circuits and local flights that began and ended at the same field.

If `airspaces` is empty (many unlicensed strips have no published airspace),
*then* fall back to a circle — 2–3 km for a small field, 8–10 km for a hub:

```json
{"type": "Circle", "coordinates": [-1.2347, 51.1936], "radius": 3000}
```

For a place that is not an airport, use `/waypoints/search?q=...` to get `lon`/`lat`.
Never invent coordinates — look them up.

## POST /query

Request fields:

| Field | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `match` | `null` | Predicate tree. `null` matches everything. |
| `end_date` | latest date with data | **Exclusive** upper bound on `start_ts`. |
| `window_days` | `7` | Window size in days back from `end_date`. **Max 7.** |
| `start_from` | `null` | Optional floor on `start_ts`. Must be before `end_date`. |
| `limit` | `100` | 1–10000 per page. |
| `cursor` | `null` | From the previous response. |
| `include_path` | `true` | **Set `false` unless you are drawing the trajectory.** |

Response: `{"flights": [...], "cursor": ..., "window_from": ...}`.

Each flight carries `flight_id`, `icao24`, `callsign`, `icao_type`,
`emitter_category`, `registration`, `model`, `year`, `operator`, `start_ts`,
`end_ts`, `start_point`, `end_point`, and `start_airport_ident` /
`end_airport_ident` (+ `_name`) matched at ingest. With `include_path: true` you
also get `path`, `timestamps`, `path_tracks`, `path_gs`, `path_vr`, `path_ias`,
`squawk_runs`, `alt_correction_ft` and `path_agl_ft`.

Note the asymmetry: airport idents come back **in results**, but you cannot
*filter* on them — filtering is geometric, as above.

## Predicates

A predicate is a JSON object with exactly one key. These are all of them:

### Spatial

**`trajectory_intersects`** — the path enters the geometry at any point.
**`trajectory_within`** — the path never leaves the geometry.

Both take the same value object:

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `geometry` | GeoJSON `Point`/`LineString`/`Polygon`/`MultiPolygon`/`GeometryCollection`, or `Circle`. |
| `altitude_min` / `altitude_max` | With `altitude_min_ref`/`altitude_max_ref`: `"ft"` (QNH-corrected feet MSL, default) or `"fl"` (flight level, pressure altitude). |
| `agl_min_ft` / `agl_max_ft` | Height above terrain. Good for "low flying". |
| `time_from` / `time_to` | ISO-8601 UTC bounds on time spent inside. |
| `squawk_codes` | Array of squawk strings, e.g. `["7000"]`. |
| `dwell_min_s` / `dwell_max_s` | Seconds spent inside the geometry. Needs `geometry`. |
| `distance_min_m` / `distance_max_m` | Path length inside the geometry. Needs `geometry`. |

Altitude, time and dwell are evaluated **simultaneously**: `dwell_min_s: 600`
with `altitude_max: 5000` means ten minutes spent inside the geometry *while
below 5000 ft*, not ten minutes inside and separately some time below.

**`endpoint_within`** — constrains the departure and/or arrival point.

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `mode` | `"start"`, `"end"`, `"either"` (start OR end), `"both"` (start AND end). Required. |
| `geometry` | As above. |
| `start_time_from` / `start_time_to` | Bounds on `start_ts`. Applied for `start`/`either`/`both`. |
| `end_time_from` / `end_time_to` | Bounds on `end_ts`. Applied for `end`/`either`/`both`. |

### Attribute

| Predicate | Value | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `icao_type` | array of ICAO type designators | `{"icao_type": ["DA40", "C172"]}` |
| `emitter_category` | array of ADS-B categories `A1`–`A7`, `B1`–`B7`, `C1`–`C3` | `{"emitter_category": ["A1"]}` |
| `callsign_prefix` | string prefix (**not** a regex) | `{"callsign_prefix": "BAW"}` |
| `registration_prefix` | string prefix | `{"registration_prefix": "G-AB"}` |
| `icao24` | array of 6-hex Mode S addresses | `{"icao24": ["4ca7b3"]}` |
| `duration` | `{"min_s": ..., "max_s": ...}` | `{"duration": {"max_s": 3600}}` |

Emitter categories worth knowing: `A1` light, `A2` small, `A3` large,
`A5` heavy, `A7` rotorcraft, `B1` glider, `B2` balloon, `B4` ultralight,
`B6` UAV.

### Boolean

`{"and": [...]}`, `{"or": [...]}`, `{"not": {...}}` — nest freely.

## Worked examples

**Light aircraft that landed at Popham, low and slow.** Resolve `EGHP` first
(above), then:

```json
{
  "match": {"and": [
    {"endpoint_within": {"mode": "end", "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[...]]]}}},
    {"emitter_category": ["A1"]}
  ]},
  "limit": 200, "include_path": false
}
```

**Where do arrivals at Popham come from?** Query as above, then read
`start_airport_ident` / `start_point` off each result.

**Helicopters below 1500 ft AGL over central London on one day:**

```json
{
  "match": {"trajectory_intersects": {
    "geometry": {"type": "Circle", "coordinates": [-0.1276, 51.5072], "radius": 15000},
    "agl_max_ft": 1500,
    "time_from": "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z",
    "time_to": "2026-09-02T00:00:00Z"
  }},
  "end_date": "2026-09-02T00:00:00Z", "window_days": 2,
  "limit": 500, "include_path": false
}
```

**Anything squawking 7700 (emergency) in the last week:**

```json
{
  "match": {"trajectory_intersects": {
    "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[-8,49],[2,49],[2,61],[-8,61],[-8,49]]]},
    "squawk_codes": ["7700"]
  }},
  "limit": 100, "include_path": false
}
```

**Gliders that stayed inside a ridge area for over an hour:**

```json
{
  "match": {"and": [
    {"emitter_category": ["B1"]},
    {"trajectory_intersects": {
      "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[...]]]},
      "dwell_min_s": 3600
    }}
  ]},
  "limit": 100, "include_path": false
}
```

## Pagination and time windows

Two separate mechanisms — this trips people up.

1. **Within a window**, page with `cursor`: if the response has a non-null
   `cursor`, repeat the *identical* request with `"cursor": <that value>`.
   Stop when `cursor` is `null`.
2. **To go further back in time**, the window has exhausted, not the data.
   Take `window_from` from the response and send it as the next request's
   `end_date`. Repeat.

So "all of last year" is a loop of up to 52 window-steps, each with its own
cursor pages. `window_days` is capped at 7 and **will not error** if you ask a
question spanning a year — you will silently get one week. Check `/data-range`,
then loop, and tell the user the period you actually covered.

## Gotchas

- **`window_days` maxes out at 7.** The single most common way to be wrong here
  is to report a week's results as if they were a year's.
- **`include_path: false`** unless you are plotting. A trajectory is thousands
  of coordinates; `{"limit": 1000}` with paths is a very large response.
- **`end_date` is exclusive** and bounds `start_ts` (departure time), not
  `end_ts`. A flight that departs 23:50 and lands 00:30 belongs to the earlier day.
- **`callsign_prefix` is a prefix, not a regex.** Callsigns are ICAO format
  (`BAW123`), not IATA (`BA123`).
- **Callsign ≠ registration.** `registration_prefix` matches an airframe's
  registration; flights with no linked airframe record never match it.
- **Identifier matching is forgiving, so don't pre-format.** `callsign_prefix`,
  `registration_prefix`, `icao_type` and `emitter_category` are all matched
  case-insensitively with hyphens ignored on both sides, so `g-abcd`, `GABCD`
  and `gAbCd` all match an aircraft registered `G-ABCD` — which matters because
  registrations are *published* with a hyphen and *broadcast* without one.
  `icao24` is lower-cased for you. Pass the identifier however the user said it.
- **`flight_id` is `icao24:start_ts_utc`** — e.g. `4ca7b3:2025-04-15T14:32:18Z`.
- **Altitude reference matters.** `"ft"` is QNH-corrected MSL; flights lacking
  correction data fall back to pressure altitude (±300 ft). `"fl"` is always
  pressure altitude. Use `"fl"` above the transition altitude, `"ft"` below.
- **Coverage is not global yet.** Call `/data-range`, and expect gaps outside
  Europe. An empty result may mean no coverage, not no flights.
- **Ground data is excluded.** Trajectories are airborne points only, so taxi
  and ground movement do not appear.
- **A 422 response includes a `hint` field** telling you what was wrong. Read it.

## Terms

Data derives from the [adsb.lol](https://adsb.lol) archive (ODbL), with
reference data from [OpenAIP](https://openaip.net). Positions are crowd-sourced
receiver data: coverage is uneven, low-level and remote flights are often
missing, and not all aircraft transmit ADS-B. Treat absence as absence of
evidence. Do not present this as a complete or authoritative record of flights.
